blocks.title: The Internet
blocks.text: The Internet is a worldwide set of interconnected computer networks where clients can request resources from servers.

blocks.title: DNS
blocks.text: The Domain Name System uses distributed servers to look up IP addresses associated with domain names.

blocks.title: Cloud storage and software
blocks.text: Cloud storage puts files on remote servers; cloud software and processing also provide services using remote computing resources.

blocks.title: Benefits and limitations
blocks.text: Cloud services support access from different devices, but depend on connectivity, service availability and secure access.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: The pupil begins with a readable domain name, not the server's numeric network address. The device queries a DNS service to find the matching IP address [1]. DNS looks up the domain [1] and returns the IP address to the client [1]. The browser connects to the web server using that address [1]. Check the sequence.

items: Internet — Worldwide system of connected networks.
DNS — Domain Name System; resolves names to IP addresses.
Domain name — Readable name used to identify an Internet service.
IP address — Address used for routing data on networks.
Cloud storage — Remote file storage accessed over a network.
